checks: UTF-16 ranges retain original bilingual narration and protect bounded abbreviation/number/URL/code/math samples.
New sessions and assistant replies freeze stable identities; legacy reads project exact old behavior without writing a migration.
Upgrade maps the old source start, preserves hints/answers/read status and retains the prior snapshot; same-command replay and stale/conflicting commands are checked.
New positional progress and speech reject missing/stale presentation metadata; real HTTP disconnect aborts speech generation.
An actual learning-code student can use only their own caption and allowed image actions; other accounts, revoked access and unknown actions are refused.
Pause and upgrade abort old/prefetched audio and late results; reply completion returns to the frozen original lesson unit.
Settings keyboard containment, opener focus restoration, sticky close control, long-token overflow and three viewport widths were inspected.
SQLite reopen and portable export retain original snapshot, upgraded units and history; PostgreSQL has a separate exact-commit CI suite.
limits: No claim of all languages or ambiguous abbreviation correctness.
No human listening assessment, physical mobile playback permissions, teacher content approval or long-term learning efficacy.
Muted timing is a reading estimate; no word-level or forced acoustic alignment.
Closing an upgrade request stops waiting; an already committed server change is recovered by read/replay rather than claimed rollback.
Full textbook/long-source coverage, course-package lifecycle, unused PDF byte cleanup, image iteration and other master-plan items remain incomplete.

The 390px zoom percentage remains crowded beside the plus control; tablet tables require horizontal scrolling. These are follow-ups for the complete touch/layout pass, not pixel-parity acceptance. Some long-token screenshots captured existing entry animation opacity and are not stable reference-diff artifacts.
